| 4f97dae | feat(web): add the design gallery built from the real views |
| 94cc9c1 | docs(web): add gallery screenshots for the direction review |

**Tests** (last run on HEAD, Vitest with jsdom)
- **96 tests passed** in 12 files.
- **Coverage:** lines 98.56% (137/139), branches 93.89% (123/131), statements 98.72%, functions 100%. The floor is 85%.
- `npm run check` (ESLint, Prettier, tsc), `npm run build` and the hygiene script all pass.
- Red then green is in the transcript for every unit. I split the primitives from the view and checked each commit's tree separately, so every commit is green on its own.

**Direction**
1. **Source:** mid-century American account ledgers and columnar pads. Pale green "eye-ease" paper, feint blue ruling, a red double margin rule, blue-black ink, a bottle-green cloth binding stamped in gilt.
2. **Palette:** light mode is the open page, dark mode is the closed binding, where the main action turns gilt. Red is only the margin rule and alert ink, so an overdue date is the one thing that shouts. The 13 colour tokens are canvas, sheet, ink, ink-muted, rule, rule-strong, margin, alert, primary, primary-strong, on-primary, focus and shade.
3. **Contrast:** every pairing meets WCAG AA in both themes. Text runs from 5.35:1 to 14.39:1, controls and focus from 3.37:1 up. A test fails the build if any pairing drops.
4. **Type:** Besley (a Clarendon revival) for headings only; Libre Franklin (a Franklin Gothic revival) for everything else, with tabular figures for dates. Both are self-hosted through @fontsource.
5. **Feel:** every row sits on a ruled line right of the red margin, with due dates in their own ruled column on wide screens. A 4px spacing grid plus a 44px touch step, corners of 2px and 4px, two shadows by role, 120ms and 220ms motion that drops to zero under reduced motion.

**Screenshots**
They are in `frontend/design/screenshots/`, 16 PNGs at 1x (4.9 MB). Each of overview, direction, tokens and task-list is shot at 390 and 1280, light and dark. I reviewed 2x crops of every state, and the page never scrolls sideways at either width.

The artifact is built to `frontend/design/dist/artifact.html` (599 KB). It is gitignored, so `npm run design:build` regenerates it, and I haven't published it.

**Decisions the brief didn't settle**
- **One `light-dark()` pair per colour.** Each colour is written once with its light and dark value side by side. The contracted selectors (`:root`, the guarded media query, `[data-theme="dark"]`) only switch `color-scheme`, so the dark palette isn't written twice. Tailwind's build polyfills `light-dark()`; switching at the root works, but a single element can't be themed on its own.
- **The default Tailwind theme is cleared.** Utilities off the scale (`p-5`, `bg-red-500`) simply don't exist.
- **Container queries instead of media queries.** The views respond to the width they're given, so a 390px gallery frame shows the real phone layout through the same component.
- **Sensors are mouse, touch (150ms press and hold) and keyboard,** one per input. A `PointerSensor` would claim every touch first and leave a `TouchSensor` doing nothing.
- **A `Link` primitive with a `NavigationProvider`** keeps the router out of views: plain clicks navigate in the app, modified clicks stay with the browser.
- **The search debounce belongs to the container.** The view is controlled by `query` and receives `searchPending`.
- **A create failure appears in the generic `failure` notice with a retry,** not as its own row state.
- **Dates use the `en-US` format** ("Overdue · Fri, Oct 16"), the page carries a dated overline, and notes are a non-null string, empty when there are none.
- **TypeScript is pinned to 6.0.3,** because typescript-eslint supports versions below 6.1.
- **The app entry `src/main.tsx` is a stub** until the router and data layer arrive.

**Folded in from the planner and your clarification**
- The CSP applies to the app build only. It emits external JS, CSS and font files, and nothing injects `<style>` tags at runtime.
- The schema rules match: title trimmed and 1 to 200 characters, notes up to 5,000, and moves sent as `onMove(taskId, afterId | null)`.
- `ErrorView` is noted for phase 2.

- **The desktop frames are mostly empty canvas,** because the spec calls for a centred reading width. The phase 2 app shell should give that space a frame.
- **The search summary wraps to two lines on desktop.**
- **The quick-add "Add a title." error is local state,** so the gallery only shows it when someone presses Add task with the field empty.
- **The keyboard reorder test stubs row sizes,** since jsdom has no layout. Real drag-and-drop on a device is left for Playwright.
- **The full task-list screenshots are very tall.** Crops per state would be easier to review in a PR.
- **Card-catalogue blue as a second accent** is something I'd explore with more time.

message.content:
The coordinator sent a message while you were working:
Tech lead review of phase 1: the direction is approved. The bookkeeper's ledger is exactly the kind of specific vintage source the brief asked for. The red margin rule, the ruled due column, Clarendon over Franklin and gilt in the dark binding all work, and the tokens and the contrast test are disciplined. Go ahead with phase 2, and fold in these fixes. The lead asked for "stellar look and premium feel", and right now desktop and phone read as well-made but plain.

**Fix in the system (tokens and primitives) so every screen inherits it:**
1. **Desk vs page hierarchy is too weak in light mode.** Canvas `#e3e9d8` and sheet `#f3f6ec` are nearly the same, so the page doesn't sit on a desk. Give the canvas more separation: a deeper or warmer desk tone, or the bottle-green binding as a band behind the page. Give the sheet a considered page edge (the existing shade token, maybe a faint second sheet beneath, or a hairline plus a soft drop). It should look like a real ledger page lying on a desk. Keep AA everywhere, and the contrast test must still pass.
2. **Desktop composition** (the biggest gap). At 1280 the list is a narrow column in an empty field. Design `AppShell` in phase 2 as the frame:
   - **Masthead:** a binding band carrying the app name set like a ledger title, with the user's email and Sign out.
   - **The page:** a sheet with a generous margin.
   - **Reading width:** around 760 to 840 px for the sheet.
   - **Ledger column headings:** a header row on wide screens ("Task" … "Due") in small caps with letter-spacing, sitting on the ruling.

   The empty canvas should read as intentional desk space around a page, not as leftover.
3. **Phone row density.** At 390 px, handle + checkbox + margin take about 110 px before the title starts, so titles wrap to 3 or 4 lines and the list gets long. Tighten it:
   - Bring the checkbox and the margin rule closer.
   - Consider moving the drag handle to the row's right edge on narrow widths. Keep a 44 px target, and keep keyboard and touch reordering working.
   - Reduce vertical padding a step.
   - Titles should mostly fit on 2 lines.
4. **Show interaction states in the gallery:**
   - hover and focus on a row and on buttons;
   - a row being dragged (lifted, with the shade token);
   - the drop indicator;
   - a checkbox mid-toggle;
   - the "Changed elsewhere" notice and the delete confirm in detail.
   A premium feel comes from these details.

**Fix in the gallery:**
5. **No side gutter.** Headings, swatch cards and frames run flush to the left edge. Add at least a 16 px gutter at all widths, and more on desktop.
6. **At phone width, the desktop frames are clipped at the right edge.** Scale each desktop frame to fit the available width (the `shown at 62.5%` approach, computed from the container), or put it in its own horizontal scroll container. The page body must never scroll sideways and nothing may be cut off.
7. **Screenshots:** also save per-state crops (one PNG per state per theme at both widths) under `frontend/design/screenshots/states/`, so the PR can be reviewed state by state. Keep the full-page ones too. Keep the total size reasonable; 1x is fine.

**Phase 2 scope, as briefed:**
- the remaining views (`SignInView`, `SignUpView`, `TaskDetailView`, `NotFoundView`, plus `ErrorView`) in all their states, and `AppShell`;
- the full gallery;
- `frontend/CLAUDE.md`;
- the CI `frontend` job;
- a final self-review against the brief.

The sign-in page is the landing page, the first thing a reviewer sees, so give it the most care: the ledger's title page, a cover plate with the binding colour and gilt. Make it memorable, but keep it restrained.

Keep the test discipline exactly as in phase 1: red then green, every commit green, no redundant tests. When you're done, run `npm run design:build` and report the artifact path and size. I'll publish it. Report in the same format as phase 1.

Address this before completing your current task.

git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
feat(web): lay the ledger page on a desk and tighten its lines

The lead's review of phase 1 found the look well made but plain. Four
fixes go into the system, so every screen inherits them.

A desk under the page. The light canvas is now a green blotter
(sheet on canvas goes from about 1.15:1 to 1.40:1). The page is one
sheet at an 800px reading width, with a hairline, a second sheet
peeking beneath it and a soft drop. Binding, gilt and on-binding
tokens are added for the masthead and the cover. A binding surface
turns the focus ring gilt, since the usual ring would fall to 1.6:1
on the green band. The contrast test covers the new pairings.

Denser lines on a phone. Rows are their own grids now, not a shared
subgrid. Narrow rows put the tick box first and the handle at the
right edge, with a smaller gap to the margin rule and one step less
padding, so most titles fit in two lines. Wide rows keep handle,
tick box, text and a ruled due column, with small-caps column heads
on the ruling.

Lift and drop. A carried row is a DragOverlay lifted on the shade
token, aria-hidden and inert. Its place in the list becomes a dashed
slot that shows where it will land. The tick box presses in and its
tick draws on, both on the duration tokens, so reduced motion stills
them.

Forceable states. Hover, focus-visible and active also match data
attributes, so the gallery can show those states on the real
components. The app never sets them.

Paths now live in one routes module that the views and the router
share.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

feat(web): add sign-in and sign-up as the ledger's title page

Sign-in is the landing page, the first screen a reviewer sees, so it
gets the most care. It is the ledger opened at its title page: the
cloth cover with the title tooled in gilt inside a blind-stamped
double frame, and the first page beside it (below it on a phone)
holding the form. AuthLayout draws that once for both screens.

CredentialsForm is the one form behind both. It validates with
credentialsSchema, the schema the API layer will use: the email is
trimmed and at most 254 characters, the password is 12 to 128
characters and never trimmed. Problems show next to their field and
clear when the field is edited, and the whole fieldset holds while
submitting. A small fieldErrors helper turns a Zod error into one
message per field, so the task form can reuse it.

The views map each failure to its copy: 401 to "don't match", 409
to "already exists" with a link to sign in instead, and no answer
to "couldn't reach the server". Field and TextArea come out of
TextField, so the label, hint and error are linked to the control
the same way everywhere.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

input.command:
python3 scripts/check_hygiene.py && git add frontend/src && git status --short && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
feat(web): add the task detail, not found and error screens

The detail screen covers every state the spec names: viewing, editing,
saving, field errors, "Changed elsewhere", the delete confirm and
not found. It reads like a ledger entry: the title with its tick box,
the due date in its tone, Status, Entered and Changed on the ruling,
and notes on ruled lines.

Editing follows D17. A save sends only the changed fields (PATCH)
with the version the edit started from (If-Match). The view
recognises its own save when the new version comes back and leaves
edit mode. A newer version that changes something under an unsaved
draft raises "Changed elsewhere" and names what changed, with "Use
the latest" or "Keep my edits", which rebases the draft so the next
save goes against the newer version. A newer version that changes
nothing visible rebases quietly. The version check uses React's
guarded "adjust state when a prop changes" pattern, not an effect.

Delete waits for InlineConfirm, built into the page because
confirm() is not usable, with focus on the safe choice. Not found
says the same thing for a missing task and someone else's, so it
never confirms another user's id. ErrorView gives the route error
boundary a message, Try again and Go to tasks.

Notice now takes a list of actions and drops its unused info tone.
Button gains danger and a buttonClass for links that act as
buttons, and EmptyState can head a page and carry a "No entry"
ledger stamp.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

# frontend

React 19 SPA in TypeScript (Vite 8, Tailwind 4, Zod 4, dnd-kit). The views and the design gallery are built; the router, TanStack Query and the fetch wrapper come with the data layer.

## Commands
```bash
npm ci                       # Node 24
npm run dev                  # the app on Vite's dev server
npm run check                # ESLint (type-checked) + prettier --check + tsc --noEmit
npm run test                 # Vitest + coverage; fails under 85% lines or branches
npm run build                # tsc, then the app into dist/
npm run design:dev           # the design gallery on Vite's dev server
npm run design:build         # the gallery as one self-contained file: design/dist/artifact.html
npm run design:screenshots   # after design:build; needs `npx playwright install chromium` once
```
Every commit passes `check`, `test` and `build`.

## Layout
- `src/styles/tokens.css`: every colour, size, radius, shadow and duration, as Tailwind `@theme` tokens. The default theme is cleared, so a utility off the scale (`p-5`, `bg-red-500`) does not exist.

## Phase 2 done: every screen built, the review fixes in, ready for you to publish

Phase 2 and all seven review fixes are committed and green on `feature/web-design-system`. Nothing is pushed and there is no PR.

**Artifact:** `/Users/ag/Documents/dev-artemis/todo-app/.claude/worktrees/agent-aff2c62ed81fa6395/frontend/design/dist/artifact.html`, 655,472 bytes (640 KB), built from HEAD. It opens with `<title>todo-app Design Gallery</title>`, has no document wrapper tags, inlines all JS, CSS and fonts, and uses no browser storage. The build fails if anything would load over the network or the file passes 16 MB. The file is gitignored; `npm run design:build` rebuilds it.

### Branch and commits (phase 2, after 94cc9c1)
| sha | subject |
|---|---|
| 97ec34a | feat(web): lay the ledger page on a desk and tighten its lines |
| 38c48d0 | feat(web): add the app shell, a binding band over the desk |
| 51dce07 | feat(web): add sign-in and sign-up as the ledger's title page |
| f51cc78 | feat(web): add the task detail, not found and error screens |
| 54d9e43 | fix(web): centre the title-page spread and give the cover its size |
| b439d8e | refactor(web): share the ledger line classes and the handle mark |
| 96887c7 | fix(web): keep the page still when the delete confirm takes focus |
| e8dfcb9 | feat(web): show every screen, state and interaction in the gallery |
| 59c441b | docs(web): add the phase 2 gallery screenshots |
| 358eb46 | docs(web): add frontend/CLAUDE.md with commands, layout and gotchas |
| 68a1d62 | ci: add the frontend job |

All 18 commits on the branch carry the trailer. Where a commit was cut from a larger working tree, I checked its staged tree in a scratch copy before committing.

### Tests (last `npm run test`)
- **151 passed in 24 files.**
- **Coverage:** lines 97.72% (258/264), branches 92.54% (211/228), statements 97.6%, functions 98.19%. The floor is 85%.
- `check`, `build`, `design:build` and the hygiene script all pass.
- Every new unit went red, then green. For the detail view's quiet-rebase test, which passed on first run, I removed its branch to show it fail, then restored it.

### Your review points
1. **Desk and page.** The light desk is now a green blotter (page on desk goes from about 1.15:1 to 1.40:1). The page has a hairline, a second sheet peeking beneath, and a soft drop shadow. New binding, gilt and on-binding tokens are in the contrast test.
2. **Desktop composition.** `AppShell` adds a binding band with the gilt "TO DO" title between double rules, the email and Sign out. The page is 800px wide on the desk, with small-caps "Task … Due" column heads on the ruling.
3. **Phone density.** On narrow screens the tick box comes first and the handle moves to the right edge (still 44px, still keyboard and touch). There's less gap before the margin rule and one step less padding, so most titles fit on two lines.
4. **Interaction states.** A new section shows line hover and keyboard focus, a carried row over its dashed drop slot, the tick box pressed and focused, and every button in rest, hover, focus and disabled, including the gilt focus ring on the band. "Changed elsewhere" and the delete confirm appear in the detail states.
5. **Gutter.** 16px on phones, 48px on desktop, on every block, so the crops keep it too.
6. **Clipped frames.** Desktop frames now scale to fit their column. At 390px the page never scrolls sideways; I also checked 320px in both themes, with nothing clipped and no console errors.
7. **Per-state crops.** 132 PNGs in `frontend/design/screenshots/states/`, plus the overview, direction, tokens and interaction sections in `frontend/design/screenshots/`. The full set is 3.7 MB (palette PNGs through `sharp`, down from 21 MB).

### Phase 2 scope
- **Views:** `SignInView`, `SignUpView` (a shared `CredentialsForm` and `AuthLayout`), `TaskDetailView`, `NotFoundView` and `ErrorView`, plus `AppShell`.
- **Sign-in** is the ledger's title page: a cloth cover in a 3:4 portrait shape with the gilt title inside a double frame, beside the first page with the form. On a phone the cover is compact and the form starts on the first screen.
- **Docs and CI:** `frontend/CLAUDE.md` is in, and the `frontend` job (npm ci, check, test, build) is added to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
- **Self-review:**
  - Only `frontend/` and `ci.yml` changed.
  - Every export has JSDoc.
  - No router, TanStack Query, MSW or fetch wrapper was added.
  - Every state the brief lists is shown through the real view.

### Direction
1. **Source:** a mid-century American bookkeeper's ledger: green eye-ease paper, feint blue ruling, a red double margin rule, blue-black ink, bottle-green cloth with gilt tooling.
2. **Palette:** light mode is the open page on a green blotter; dark mode is the closed binding, where actions turn gilt. Red appears only as the margin rule and as alert ink.
3. **Type:** Besley (a Clarendon revival) for headings and the gilt title only; Libre Franklin for everything read at length, with tabular figures for dates.
4. **Feel:** a page lying on a desk under a binding band. Ruled lines, a ruled due column, ruled notes, a "No entry" stamp on not found.
5. **Restraint:** near-square corners, two shadows by role, 120ms and 220ms motion that drops to zero under reduced motion.

### Decisions the brief didn't settle
- **Gallery-only state attributes.** Hover, focus-visible and active also match `data-hover`, `data-focus-visible` and `data-active`, so the gallery can show those states on the real components. That's three lines in `index.css`; the app never sets them.
- **Scripted gallery states.** States that live in a view's local state (editing, field errors, saving, "Changed elsewhere", the delete confirm, a failed save) are reached by `Scripted`. It presses and fills the real view the way a user would, then changes props the way a container would.
- **The detail view recognises its own save.** When a newer version arrives that matches what it submitted, it leaves edit mode. This uses React's guarded "adjust state when a prop changes" pattern, which passes the React Compiler lint rules. A newer version that changes nothing visible rebases the draft quietly, so there's no needless 412.
- **Saves send only the changed fields** (PATCH) with the version the edit started from (If-Match), as `onSave(taskId, changes, version)`.
- **Failures are typed unions, and the view owns the copy:** `SignInFailure` is `"wrong-credentials" | "unreachable"`; `SignUpFailure` is `"email-taken" | "unreachable"`.
- **`userSchema` is `{ id, email }` only.** Zod drops extra keys, so a `createdAt` from the API would do no harm.
- **Paths live in one `routes` module**, shared by the views and the router to come.
- **`ErrorView`'s callbacks are `onRetry` and `onGoToTasks`.**
- **`Notice` lost its unused `info` tone;** every notice in the app is an alert.
- **`sharp` is added as a dev dependency,** only for compressing the screenshots.

### Weaknesses
- **The view tests run in jsdom, so they never see real CSS.** Layout and theme correctness rest on visual QA, not tests; the Playwright layer should cover the phone layout and a real drag.
- **Theming is root-only.** Tailwind polyfills `light-dark()`, so no single block can be themed differently from the page.
- **Gallery-only CSS ships in the app's stylesheet.** The forced-state attributes and `sharp` exist only for the gallery.
- **At 390px the desktop frames scale to about 28%,** too small to read; the phone frame is the one to review there.
- **Some colour pairs only look plausible.** The green, gilt and red values are drawn from the source but not matched to a physical ledger.

- **Theming is root-only.** Tailwind polyfills `light-dark()`, so no single block can be themed differently from the page.
- **Gallery-only CSS ships in the app's stylesheet.** The forced-state attributes and `sharp` exist only for the gallery.
- **At 390px the desktop frames scale to about 28%,** too small to read; the phone frame is the one to review there.
- **Some colour pairs only look plausible.** The green, gilt and red values are drawn from the source but not matched to a physical ledger.

# frontend

React 19 SPA in TypeScript (Vite 8, Tailwind 4, Zod 4, dnd-kit). The views and the design gallery are built; the router, TanStack Query and the fetch wrapper come with the data layer.

## Commands

```bash
npm ci                       # Node 24
npm run dev                  # the app on Vite's dev server
npm run check                # ESLint (type-checked) + prettier --check + tsc --noEmit
npm run test                 # Vitest + coverage; fails under 85% lines or branches
npm run build                # tsc, then the app into dist/
npm run design:dev           # the design gallery on Vite's dev server
npm run design:build         # the gallery as one self-contained file: design/dist/artifact.html
npm run design:screenshots   # after design:build; needs `npx playwright install chromium` once
```

Every commit passes `check`, `test` and `build`.

## Layout

- `src/styles/tokens.css`: every colour, size, radius, shadow and duration, as Tailwind `@theme` tokens. The default theme is cleared, so a utility off the scale (`p-5`, `bg-red-500`) does not exist.
- `src/styles/index.css`: Tailwind, fonts, the `binding` and `ruled` utilities, and the hover, focus-visible and active variants the gallery can force.
- `src/components/ui/`: primitives. `src/components/`: compositions (`AppShell`, `AuthLayout`, `CredentialsForm`).
- `src/views/`: one view per screen. Props in, JSX out: no fetching, no router hooks, every intent leaves as a callback. Only local affordances (a draft, an open confirm) live in `useState`.
- `src/lib/`: pure helpers, `routes.ts`, and `schema/` (Zod, shared by forms and the API layer).
- `src/test/fixtures.ts`: the sample data and view props that both the tests and the gallery use.
- `design/`: the gallery, a second Vite entry. `screens.tsx` lists every state; `Scripted` drives a view the way a user would to reach states held in local state. `screenshots/` is committed.

## Gotchas

- `light-dark()` colours are polyfilled by Tailwind's Lightning CSS pass, so a theme switches only at the root (`color-scheme` on `:root`). Light-mode focus on the green band is too faint, so anything on the band sits in the `binding` utility, which turns the ring gilt.
- Layout responds to container width (`@wide:`), not the viewport. A view needs an `@container` ancestor; `Page`, `AppShell` and `AuthLayout` provide one.
- The gallery build roots Vite at `design/`, so `index.css` names `src/` and `design/` as Tailwind sources explicitly.
- Vitest stubs CSS imports; only `tokens.css` is processed, so the token tests can read it.
- `data-hover`, `data-focus-visible` and `data-active` exist for the gallery only. Never set them in app code.
- The design build inlines everything; the app build must not inline anything (the nginx CSP is `'self'` only).

- `src/lib/`: pure helpers, `routes.ts`, and `schema/` (Zod, shared by forms and the API layer).
- `src/test/fixtures.ts`: the sample data and view props that both the tests and the gallery use.
- `design/`: the gallery, a second Vite entry. `screens.tsx` lists every state; `Scripted` drives a view the way a user would to reach states held in local state. `screenshots/` is committed.

## Gotchas

- `light-dark()` colours are polyfilled by Tailwind's Lightning CSS pass, so a theme switches only at the root (`color-scheme` on `:root`). Light-mode focus on the green band is too faint, so anything on the band sits in the `binding` utility, which turns the ring gilt.
- Layout responds to container width (`@wide:`), not the viewport. A view needs an `@container` ancestor; `Page`, `AppShell` and `AuthLayout` provide one.
- The gallery build roots Vite at `design/`, so `index.css` names `src/` and `design/` as Tailwind sources explicitly.
- Vitest stubs CSS imports; only `tokens.css` is processed, so the token tests can read it.
- `data-hover`, `data-focus-visible` and `data-active` exist for the gallery only. Never set them in app code.
- The design build inlines everything; the app build must not inline anything (the nginx CSP is `'self'` only).

</system-reminder>

The lead made these hard requirements. This table shows where each one lives and why it belongs there. It is what the instructions walkthrough uses, and what reviewers will probe. It lists only places where the construct earns its keep.

| What `TASK.md` asks for | Backend: where, and why there | Frontend: where, and why there |
|---|---|---|
| Higher-order functions | `Depends(get_session, scope="function")`, `Depends(get_current_user)` and `Depends(require_trusted_origin)`: FastAPI takes these functions and composes each request from them, so settings, the session and the user reach a route without globals. `Hasher.hash` passes the hashing function to `asyncio.to_thread` behind a semaphore. The rank core passes predicates and step functions to `takewhile`, `reduce` and `all`. | `createQueryClient({ onUnauthenticated })` takes the redirect as a function, so the query client never imports the router. `queryFn: ({ signal }) => listTasks(q, signal)`, `retry: (count, error) => …` and `setQueriesData(key, updater)` are all functions handed to TanStack. `optimisticListUpdate(client, apply)` (§ 4.4) builds the shared `onMutate` for toggle, move and delete: three callers, so it removes real repetition. |
| Function composition | A request flows middleware → dependencies → router → service → repository, each a small function the next one calls. `search_pattern(normalize_query(q))`. `rank_between` is built from `split_rank`, `increment` or `decrement`, and `midpoint`. Python has no compose operator and nesting small functions is the idiom, so there is no `compose()` helper. | `apiRequest` is `fetch`, then a status check, then `schema.parse` (or `errorEnvelopeSchema.safeParse` into an `ApiError`). Each page container composes hooks into props for one view. A save runs `diffDraft`, then `taskPatchSchema.parse`, then `updateTask`. |
| Correct data structures | `STATUS_BY_ERROR: Mapping[type[DomainError], tuple[int, str]]`: one handler finds any error's status in O(1), and reviewers check one table. `DIGIT_VALUE` (a read-only mapping, not `str.index`), `DIGIT_SET` (a frozenset, for membership) and `RANK_RULES` (a tuple: fixed and ordered). `TaskChanges` is a `TypedDict` for a partial update. In Postgres, the unique index on `(owner_id, rank)` is both the ordered access path and the uniqueness guard, and `citext` makes email equality case-insensitive inside the index itself. | Query keys are hierarchical tuples, so `invalidateQueries(taskKeys.lists())` reaches every cached search at once. `ApiErrorCode` is an `as const` object: a closed set with an exhaustive `switch`. Dismissed notices are a `ReadonlySet` (membership). Task lists stay arrays because order is the point. |
| map, filter, reduce, apply | `apply_patch` is a dict comprehension over `dataclasses.fields(patch)` that filters out `UNSET`. Validation `details` come from a list comprehension over Pydantic's errors. `reduce` carries the carry in `step_digits`. "Apply" here is function application: `to_thread(fn, *args)`, and FastAPI calling the dependency functions. | Toggle: `items.map(t => t.id === id ? { ...t, completed } : t)`. Delete: `items.filter(t => t.id !== id)`. Notices: `filter` to failed mutations, then `reduce` to the newest. `moveAfter`: `findIndex`, then `toSpliced`. Server field errors: `Object.fromEntries(details.map(d => [d.field, d.message]))`. |
| Immutability | Frozen Pydantic models (`frozen=True`), frozen dataclasses (`TaskPatch`, `SessionClaims`, `Hasher`), tuples for fixed data and `MappingProxyType` for `DIGIT_VALUE`. No function mutates its input, and the rank functions build new strings. | `readonly` types, and `toSpliced`, `with` and spread instead of `splice`, `sort` or assignment. Cache updaters return new arrays, which TanStack's structural sharing depends on. The draft is replaced, never edited in place. |
| Declarative over imperative | `match (lower, upper)` in `rank_between`. Guards declared in SQL (unique indexes, `CHECK`s) rather than checked in Python. The error map as data. | The router as a route table, the Zod schemas that forms validate against, and the k6 budgets as threshold data. |
| Async through high-level abstractions | Async SQLAlchemy sessions with `async with session.begin()`, `asyncio.to_thread` with `asyncio.Semaphore`, `asyncio.timeout` in `/readyz`, logging through a `QueueHandler` thread, and `asyncio.TaskGroup` in the race tests | TanStack Query for every request: caching, cancellation through `AbortSignal`, optimistic updates with rollback, and a mutation `scope` that runs reorders one at a time. Never `useEffect` plus `fetch`. |

import re
import subprocess
import sys

cutoff = "2026-10-05T23:59:59"
pkg = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
pins = {**pkg["dependencies"], **pkg["devDependencies"]}
stable = re.compile(r"^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$")

    return tuple(int(part) for part in version.split("."))


for name, pinned in sorted(pins.items()):
    times = json.loads(subprocess.run(["npm", "view", name, "time", "--json"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout)
    eligible = [v for v, t in times.items() if stable.match(v) and t <= cutoff]
    same_major = [v for v in eligible if v.split(".")[0] == pinned.split(".")[0]]
    best = max(same_major or eligible, key=key)
    flag = "ok" if times.get(pinned, "") <= cutoff else "TOO NEW"
    print(f"{name:32} {pinned:10} {times.get(pinned, '?')[:10]}  {flag:8} latest<=cutoff (same major): {best} ({times[best][:10]})")

# TypeScript

- `strict` is on in `tsconfig.json`. No `any`, no `as unknown as`, no `@ts-ignore`, no non-null `!` to silence a real `undefined`. Named exports. Function components with hooks; no classes, except `Error` subclasses (`ApiError`), which `instanceof` narrowing and TanStack Query's typed errors need.
- Every boundary is a Zod schema under `src/lib/schema/`: API responses, form data, storage, URL params. `parse`, or `safeParse` with a typed error path, right after reading; field access on the parsed value. Types come from the schema with `z.infer`, never written twice.
- Every API call goes through the one fetch wrapper in `src/lib/api/`, which sends the session cookie (same origin), parses the body and turns error bodies into a typed `ApiError`. No bare `fetch` in components or hooks.
- Domain types live in `src/types/` or next to their schema, reachable from any layer. Never define a cross-cutting type inside `components/`.
- Enums are `as const` objects, not `enum`. Use the typed constant, never the string literal.
- Discriminated unions are closed. Switch on the discriminant, and make the switch exhaustive with a `never` check.
- Environment values are read through one module, never raw `import.meta.env` in components. Build-time values are public; a secret never goes there.
- JSDoc: a summary line on every exported function, component and type. `@param` and `@returns` only when they say something the signature does not.
- Logic lives in exported pure helpers a test can reach (filtering, ordering, formatting), not inline in markup.
- Filenames are kebab-case. Tests sit next to the code they test as `<name>.test.ts(x)`.
- `npm run check` (ESLint, Prettier check, `tsc --noEmit`) is the gate.

## Q-17 and Q-18 are applied in two green commits

Both items are on `feature/web-design-system`, on top of 430231f. Nothing is rebased or pushed, and the tree is clean.

| sha | subject |
|---|---|
| **b86f7a2** | build(web): pin dependencies to releases at least two weeks old |
| **33a8278** | fix(web): accept any server-validated email in the user schema |

Both carry the trailer.

**Tests** (last `npm run test`): 152 passed in 24 files, one more than before (the Q-18 test). Coverage: lines 97.72% (258/264), branches 92.54% (211/228), statements 97.6%, functions 98.19%. `npm run check`, `npm run build`, `npm run design:build` and `python3 scripts/check_hygiene.py` all pass.

### Pin table (cutoff: published on or before 2026-10-05)
I checked every date with `npm view <pkg> time --json`. The other 19 pins were already inside the rule; TypeScript 6.0.3 (2026-04-16) is kept as you said.

| Package | Old | New | New one published |
|---|---|---|---|
| react | 19.3.1 | 19.3.0 | 2026-09-09 |
| react-dom | 19.3.1 | 19.3.0 | 2026-09-09 |
| zod | 4.6.7 | 4.6.5 | 2026-09-13 |
| @testing-library/user-event | 14.6.8 | 14.6.7 | 2026-09-02 |
| @types/node | 24.19.2 | 24.19.1 | 2026-10-01 |
| vite | 8.3.4 | **8.3.2** | 2026-10-01 |
| vitest | 5.0.5 | 5.0.3 | 2026-09-30 |
| @vitest/coverage-v8 | 5.0.5 | 5.0.3 | 2026-09-30 |
| eslint | 10.13.0 | 10.12.0 | 2026-10-02 |
| typescript-eslint | 8.71.2 | 8.71.1 | 2026-10-05 |
| jsdom | 30.1.3 | 30.1.1 | 2026-09-22 |
| playwright | 1.64.1 | 1.63.0 | 2026-09-04 |
| prettier | 3.9.10 | 3.9.9 | 2026-09-23 |
| vite-plugin-singlefile | 2.3.4 | **2.3.4 (kept)** | 2026-10-17 |

All pins are exact, with no `^`.

### Where I departed from the plan's § 13.5
- **vite is 8.3.2, not 8.3.3.** 8.3.3 is from 2026-10-06, a day past the cutoff. Its changelog's only `fs.serve` entry is "check `fs.serve` for `?vite-wasm-instance`" on the dev server. There's no advisory behind it and the app uses no WebAssembly, so it doesn't justify going past the rule.
- **vite-plugin-singlefile stays at 2.3.4, not 2.3.3.** 2.3.3 depends on `micromatch`, and through it on `braces`. `braces` has a high advisory (GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm, a denial of service) with no fixed release. 2.3.4 replaces `micromatch` with `picomatch`, the only way to clear it. With 2.3.3, every `npm ci` (including CI) would report 3 high-severity vulnerabilities. With 2.3.4 the audit is clean. In practice we weren't exposed, since `braces` only expanded our own build-time patterns.

### The lockfile needed a newer npm once
The default npm 11.5.1 crashes while building this dependency tree. The error is "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut')" in arborist's peer-set loading. It comes from vitest's optional peers pulling in a newer vitest, and it happened even with no lockfile at all. I regenerated the lockfile once with `npx npm@11.21.0 install` (that npm is from 2026-09-30, so it passes the same rule). Then I deleted `node_modules` and ran a clean `npm ci` with the default npm 11.5.1: it installs, the audit finds 0 vulnerabilities, and every top-level version matches its pin.

Because the lockfile was regenerated from scratch, transitive dependencies are re-resolved too. The two-week rule was applied to our direct pins only.

### Q-18
`userSchema.email` is now `z.string().min(1)`. `credentialsSchema` keeps its email check for the forms. The new test was red with `z.email()` ("Invalid email address") and is green now, parsing `josé@exämple.com`.

None refreshed, because nothing visual changed. I reshot all 148 with Playwright 1.63's Chromium and compared pixels against the committed set. All are the same size. 147 have no differing pixels; `task-detail-saving-390-light` differs on 0.019% of pixels, from Chromium anti-aliasing.
